findings.where: Title-block bar at the top, the DRAWING MMM-GA-001 and SCALE NTS cells beside PROFILE / ARTICLES / BLOG / CONTACT (desktop: the same row; phone: the top row beside the logo, above the nav row)
findings.fault: The drawing-number and scale cells are plain text that does nothing, but they sit in the nav row in the same ruled cells, light type and spaced capitals as the four menu links. Nothing marks them as labels, so they look like two more menu items. Clicking 'MMM-GA-001' does nothing.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer scanning the top bar for where to go next. They would read six menu items, try the drawing number expecting a page (projects? a CV?), get nothing, and wonder whether the menu is broken.

findings.where: Nav bar, CONTACT link (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: CONTACT is the menu's route to the page's one action, but it goes to '#' and does nothing. The working route, WRITE TO MARK, is a mailto link. A visitor who reaches for the menu's Contact, the usual place to look, finds a dead link.
findings.who_objects: A visitor ready to get in touch who goes to the nav first, as most do on an advisor's site. They hit a dead link at the moment of intent and may think the site is unfinished.

findings.where: First-screen section drawing, the amber hatched third bay; the palette card SODIUM AMBER ('daylight in the drawing, and the one action')
findings.fault: Sodium amber is set as the primary action's colour (WRITE TO MARK), and the large amber bay in the drawing above uses it too. The palette gives the colour both jobs. So in the first screen amber means both 'decoration' and 'act here', and the button loses its claim to be the only amber thing that acts.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor taking in the first screen. Their eye goes to the amber bay before the button, and the colour no longer reliably signals the action. On the later inner pages, where Angélique adds drawings or highlights, amber would keep competing with the button.

findings.where: Motion sketch, the REPLAY THE CUT control
findings.fault: This control is a button that replays the animation in place, but it looks like a text link: underlined spaced capitals, the same treatment as the article's link to the 'Streamlining the PPP Process' lecture. One look carries two functions, act here and go somewhere, and the underline is the link's signifier.
findings.who_objects: Mark or Angélique reviewing the tile, and later a visitor. They would expect the underlined label to open a page or file, not replay the drawing. The layout round would also inherit an ambiguous button style.

findings.where: Article specimen, the boxed 'Streamlining the PPP Process' attachment (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The attachment is drawn as a bordered card holding a title, the type (Lecture) and 'PDF', so the whole box looks like one tappable item. Only the underlined title is a link. A click on the box's empty area or on 'Lecture · 2026-04-23 · PDF' does nothing.
findings.who_objects: A reader on a phone who taps the card's lower half, the 'PDF' label, to open the lecture and gets nothing. This pattern repeats on every post where Angélique attaches a PDF.

findings.where: First screen, the double rule under the heading MARK M. MOSELEY
findings.fault: The heading has a double underline cut to the width of the name, and an underline is the page's link signifier (the article link and REPLAY THE CUT both use it). The name reads faintly as a link to a profile page, but it is static.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who wants Mark's background and clicks his name expecting the profile. Nothing happens.
